minutes.headline: Water commissioners reviewed the draft budget, targeted Feb 8 for final numbers, and heard a lead service line grant plan.
minutes.summary: The board approved the minutes of two January 4 meetings, then walked through the draft maintenance and operating budget with rate increase revenue. They also discussed the conservation filing for well pump testing, a state permit rejection on the Mass Ave water main, the clerk's raise request, the lead service line rule and funding, and a customer's finance charges. No budget vote was taken; the board will revisit at a meeting in two weeks, with a possible executive session first.

budget_items.what_was_said: Loan payments dropped as a water tank loan payment ended, lowering interest slightly. Insurance, Aflac and life insurance expected to stay about the same.
Legal costs rose because of more outreach to counsel on the projects.
The new retirement figure had not arrived; the board suggested estimating from past increases.
Budgeted for five employees but only four take it, so the existing number should cover it.
Large jump in maintenance driven by chemicals and utilities; the rate increase was meant to cover this.
The rate increase is expected to bring in roughly an additional amount per quarter; current-year spending is running above the budget set last year.

what_happened.line: The Water District board reviewed the draft maintenance and operating budget and set a tentative target of February 8 to have it ready for posting.
No budget vote was taken; the board plans an executive session on employee salaries at the start of its next meeting, in two weeks.
The board discussed a state permit rejection on the Mass Ave water main, and the superintendent will ask Stantec about alternatives to the soil borings the state requested.
The board heard that state revolving fund programs may offer principal forgiveness grants for the lead service line inventory, and an article at town meeting may be needed.
A customer's finance charge request was deferred to the next meeting after staff review, and the minutes of two January 4 meetings were approved.

why_it_matters: The draft budget, with rate increase revenue, feeds the warrant for the March annual meeting, so water bills and the article residents vote on both depend on the numbers set in February.
Lead service line inventory work and the Mass Ave main permit could bring costs, or state grant money, that may need a town meeting article and a vote.
watch_next: Target of February 8 for the final budget, to be posted by the 10th ahead of the March 25 annual meeting, with the Worcester Regional retirement figure still outstanding.
Next meeting in two weeks, starting with a possible executive session on salaries.
